meaning:
ὑψόω, -ῶ
(ὕψος), [in LXX chiefly for רוּם, also for גָּבַהּ, נָשָׂא, etc. ;]
to lift or raise up: with accusative, Jhn.3:14 8:28 12:32, 34; ἕως τ. οὐρανοῦ, figuratively, pass., Mat.11:23, Luk.10:15. Metaphorical, to exalt, uplift: Act.2:33 5:31, 2Co.11:7, Jas.4:10, 1Pe.5:6; opposite to ταπεινῶ, Luk.1:52; ἑαυτόν, Mat.23:12, Luk.4:11 18:14 (cf. ὑπερ-υψόω).†
(AS)

He has put down princes from their thrones, and has exalted the lowly.
As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up,
Being therefore exalted by the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, he has poured out this, which you now see…
Or did I commit a sin in humbling myself that you might be exalted, because I preached to you God’s Good News free of charge?
Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.
